terms.definition: The amount of matter an object is made of.
terms.function: Names how much 'stuff' exists, in kilograms, no matter where the object is.
terms.whereItIs: The rock pile and the standard kg cubes that balance it.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the 'm' in F = ma and the thing gravity pulls on.
Gives every amount of matter a standard number; one kg is roughly a liter of water.
terms.whereItIs: The labelled standard cubes in the right pan.

terms.definition: The property that mass doesn't change when gravity or location changes.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what separates mass from weight, which is location-dependent.
terms.whereItIs: The readout that holds steady through the Earth→Moon drag.

terms.definition: A device that measures mass by comparing two amounts of matter on a beam.
terms.whyItMatters: Unlike a spring scale it compares matter directly, so the Moon can't fool it.
